findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: world_challenge, compute_generate, compute_budget · Private data: build_transaction, get_duties, world_challenge, world_enter, world_move, world_leave, get_tasks, compute_generate, compute_rent, compute_status, compute_stop, compute_budget · Public sink: build_transaction, compute_generate, compute_rent · Destructive: build_transaction, get_duties, get_tasks.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: world_challenge, compute_generate, compute_budget · Private data: build_transaction, get_duties, world_challenge, world_enter, world_move, world_leave, get_tasks, compute_generate, compute_rent, compute_status, compute_stop, compute_budget · Public sink: build_transaction, compute_generate, compute_rent · Destructive: build_transaction, get_duties, get_tasks

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "build_transaction" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
